description:
Found by s527b (2026-10-25) while explaining an emission-ab DIFF.

`./pcl --cache-info` on a tree with vendor/PPI:
    PPI sources: /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/PPI.pm (95 files)
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp's toolchain stamp (task #1843, "THE TOOLCHAIN IS PART OF THE COMPILER") locates PPI through P-FIND-MODULE-IN-INC, i.e. the PROGRAM's @INC -- and s527a keeps vendor/PPI/lib OUT of the program's @INC on purpose (PCLPaths::program_inc drops $Pl::VendorPPI::LIB).  So the stamp walks the system PPI 1.291, which pl2cl no longer uses, and a re-vendor (tools/vendor-ppi) changes the token stream without changing the cache key.  The compiler-root walk covers Pl/**.pm + pl2cl only.

Consequence: a cached .lisp of a MODULE transpiled before a re-vendor is served after it.  Measured case (s527b): lib/Hash/Util.pm line 299 `%{ $s->{d} } = ();` after a for block -- with PPI pcl@8955ba30 the statement is DROPPED (dies at run time: `%h = ()` on a lock_keys hash dies); with pcl@29cb43ae it compiles.  Without a generation bump or a Pl/ edit, a warm cache keeps the dying transpile.  s527b bumps *pcl-cache-generation* for its own emission change, which re-keys everything this once; the hole stays for every later re-vendor.

Fix (cl/, not s527b's layer): the stamp's PPI walk should resolve the PPI the COMPILER loads -- <compiler root>/vendor/PPI/lib/PPI.pm when present (Pl::VendorPPI's rule: unless PCL_SYSTEM_PPI=1), else @INC as now -- or include vendor/PPI/UPSTREAM's lib-tree line in the material.  Guard: --cache-info names vendor/PPI/lib/PPI.pm; a touch of a vendored PPI file changes `compiler stamp:`.


=== s528 (Fable): CLOSED BY REFERENCE -- the same finding is #3921 (filed by s527a, s527); the fix is ruled there (s527b does it: %p-ppi-files stamps <root>/vendor/PPI/lib when present and PCL_SYSTEM_PPI is unset, else the @INC PPI; --cache-info says which).
subject: The module-cache key stamps the SYSTEM PPI, not vendor/PPI: since s527a a re-vendor does not re-key cached module transpiles (#1843's hole, reopened)
